equation_request.abstract: Continuous time quantum walks provide an important framework for designing new algorithms and modelling quantum transport and state transfer problems. Often, the graph representing the structure of a problem contains certain symmetries that confine the dynamics to a smaller subspace of the full Hilbert space. In this work, we use invariant subspace methods, that can be computed systematically using Lanczos algorithm, to obtain the reduced set of states that encompass the dynamics of the problem at hand without the specific knowledge of underlying symmetries. First, we apply this method to obtain new instances of graphs where the spatial quantum search algorithm is optimal: complete graphs with broken links and complete bipartite graphs, in particular, the star graph. These examples show that regularity and high-connectivity are not needed to achieve optimal spatial search. We also show that this method considerably simplifies the calculation of quantum transport efficiencies. Furthermore, we observe improved efficiencies by removing a few links from highly symmetric graphs. Finally, we show that this reduction method also allows us to obtain an upper bound for the fidelity of a single qubit transfer on an XY spin network.

specification.problem: Use invariant subspace (Lanczos) reduction of continuous-time quantum walks on symmetric graphs to obtain the reduced state set confining the dynamics, and apply it to spatial search (complete graphs with broken links, complete bipartite/star graphs), quantum transport efficiency, and an upper bound on single-qubit transfer fidelity on an XY spin network.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Conceptual reconstruction of the Lanczos-based invariant-subspace reduction for a continuous-time quantum walk, with a tiny finite illustrative instance of spatial search. Specific graph sizes, results and numerical values are not in the abstract.

specification.initial_state: Assumed seed |psi_0>, e.g. uniform superposition over vertices for spatial search; the abstract does not specify it.

steps.description: Choose graph Hamiltonian H (with oracle term for search) and seed state |psi_0>.
Run Lanczos from |psi_0> to build orthonormal basis |q_k> and tridiagonal reduced H of dimension m.
Evolve under e^{-iHt} in the reduced basis, tracking amplitudes c_k(t).

specification.measurement: For spatial search, measure in the vertex basis at an evolution time t and take the probability of the marked vertex, |c_target(t)|^2 from the reduced amplitudes. For transport, the efficiency is the population absorbed at a sink or target; for XY spin transfer, the fidelity is the overlap on the target site. Exact observables are assumed, not given in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Scan t to find the time maximizing success probability, transport efficiency or fidelity. Compare across graphs (e.g. with links removed) and scaling with N to judge optimality. The fidelity upper bound is derived analytically in the reduced space (not specified in the abstract).
assumptions: Standard Lanczos/Krylov formulation assumed for the reduction.
